summary: High throttle rate observed during scheduled API key rotations; customer asking about quota accounting on invoice
description:
Issue summary: Customer BrightPath Health reports elevated throttling that starts exactly during their scheduled rolling API-key rotation window. They see a spike of 429 responses across multiple short-lived worker processes and report that the spike corresponds to an unexpected drop in successful request counts in their app and a mismatch on their monthly usage report. Impact: Customer-facing search and document ingestion pipelines experience partial failures for ~6 minutes during each rotation; degradation repeats during each scheduled rotation window. They are concerned both about reliability and whether the 429s will increase billed usage.

Environment: Dedicated pool, prod, us-east. Customer uses multiplexed websocket connections plus short-lived keys (rotated every 5 minutes by an internal scheduler). They run ~120 concurrent worker processes across 6 hosts; each worker opens 3 persistent websocket sessions and performs infilling/prefetch calls.

Steps to reproduce (customer provided):
1) Configure short-lived API keys with TTL=5m and automated rotation that creates new key then instructs workers to swap.
2) Workers reconnect sockets immediately after receiving new key and reopen streams.
3) At rotation boundary, observe sudden 10-20% 429 rate for 1-6 minutes then gradual recovery.

Observed behavior: 1) 429 burst at rotation boundaries correlated with simultaneous reconnects. 2) Server trace shows per-key token bucket resets and edge-layer reconnection counters spike. 3) Customer's billing export shows fewer accepted requests than attempted, but their invoiced token counts are higher than the number of successful requests they see internally, creating confusion.

Expected behavior: Rolling key swap should not cause tenant-level throttling if aggregate tenant usage remains within quota; reconnections should not double-count transient tokens or force tenant-level exhaustion. Billing should align with accepted (served) tokens, not failed/429 attempts.

Attachments/logs: Customer provided rate graphs, a representative request trace header (x-tenant-id and x-api-key-hash), and a CSV of per-minute 429 counts for the window. Logs show repeated new connection handshakes from the same tenant within a 30s window.
steps_to_reproduce: Schedule a rotation of short-lived keys (TTL 5m) with all workers swapping within the same 30s window
Have each worker immediately reconnect websocket streams after swap
Observe tenant-level token-bucket exhaustion and 429s for 1-6 minutes
observed_behavior: Burst of 429s aligned with rotation windows
Edge-layer token bucket resets visible in logs
Billing export shows token counts that customer says do not map cleanly to successful requests
expected_behavior: Rolling key swap should preserve tenant quota accounting and avoid tenant-level throttling
Billing should only include accepted requests/tokens

2026-03-10 10:02 - SRE (Jordan Li): Noted spike correlates with websocket reconnect flood; suspect per-key short TTL causing transient duplication of counts at the edge

2026-03-10 11:25 - Billing (Erin O'Neil): Confirmed preliminary: invoices are based on accepted tokens but export aggregation window can make it appear higher if retries and accepted late-arriving tokens aggregate differently; will reconcile with product metrics
2026-03-11 08:42 - Ravi Patel: Requested packet-level pcap from customer and a timeline of key issuance events; asked Eng to look at rate-limiter counters
investigation_notes: Edge token-bucket service emits a reset on explicit reconnects which can temporarily attribute tokens to ephemeral key bucket state — hypothesis: simultaneous reconnects cause momentary tenant accounting skew as per-key buckets and tenant buckets are reconciled
We observed a pattern where newly created keys are briefly unrecognized by some edge replicas leading to reconnects being retried and counted against tenant concurrency windows
Dedicated pool autoscaler not implicated; no GPU shortage alarms during windows
Related internal bug: race in token-bucket initialization in rate-limiter when key hash not present in in-memory cache on first use on a replica (investigating commit history)
temp_workarounds: Stagger key rotations across worker fleet by random jitter (recommended immediate mitigation)
Increase short-lived key TTL to 15m to reduce rotation frequency while we triage
Implement client-side exponential backoff for reconnects with small jitter at rotation boundary
action_items: SRE/Edge to reproduce in staging with simulated short-lived key rotation across 50 clients
Rate-limiter team to add guard to avoid double-counting during initial key registration on a replica
Billing to produce reconciled report showing only accepted tokens vs attempted requests for the customer's billing window
resolution: Workaround accepted by customer: BrightPath applied staggered rotations and increased key TTL to 15m; client jitter implemented. Eng deployed a guard in staging to prevent token-bucket initialization from creating transient tenant pressure; full fix targeted for next minor release (link to PR). Billing reconciled the invoice for the affected month and confirmed only accepted tokens are charged; customer invoice adjusted for the investigation window. Follow-up: recommend guidance doc updates and console warning when many short-lived keys are issued within a narrow window.
